claim: First chunk stays one sentence; later chunks batch two, so the synthesiser carries intonation across the boundary instead of resetting at every period.

before.text: This is the opening sentence.||It continues here.||Then a third thought arrives.||And finally it closes.

after.text: This is the opening sentence.||It continues here. Then a third thought arrives.||And finally it closes.

listen_check.instructions: Play before.wav then after.wav. Both are ~6.06 s — total duration is expected to be near-identical, because merging two synthesis calls does not change how much speech there is. What to listen for is the boundary between sentences two and three: does the after side carry intonation across it instead of resetting flat? Duration and loudness cannot measure this; only a listener can.

segmentation.note: Each '||' is an independent synthesis call, concatenated as raw PCM — the same thing the pipeline's player does. Synthesizing the reply as one blob would hide the chunk boundaries under test.
after_segments: It continues here. Then a third thought arrives.

first_audio_claim.benchmark_result: cannot resolve — FirstAudioReadyElapsed moved +601 ms on synth-01 and -437 ms on synth-03 between consecutive runs, in opposite directions. That is the end-to-end noise floor recorded in FINDINGS F4, not an effect of this change.
first_audio_claim.structural_argument: The opening chunk is unchanged by construction: chunking still emits exactly one sentence first (firstChunkSentences = 1), so the first synthesis call receives byte-identical text to before. Only chunks two onward batch.
first_audio_claim.conclusion: The claim is carried by the tests, not by the benchmark. Stated this way deliberately: reporting the noisy numbers as confirmation would be overclaiming.
